actions.text: Fired on Enemy target at 2100 Weather Good
actions.note: Battery C's own morning report, 2 mi E of Oran. Its only firing at Oran. The report says "target", not aircraft: for an anti-aircraft gun battery that means aircraft (inferred). No time zone typed. No Oran paper of these days is on Gallica. L'Écho d'Alger of 21 and 22 Jan 1943 (gallica:bpt6k7586936d, gallica:bpt6k7586937t) has no raid on Oran; on 22 Jan it reports alerts at Algiers "dans la soirée du 20 au 21 Janvier": the raiders met "un violent barrage de D.C.A.", a few bombs, little damage. That was Algiers, about 400 km east; Oran was raided that night, by the Italian side's account: the Italian Supreme Command's Bulletin no. 971, issued the afternoon of 21 Jan (La Stampa, 22 Jan, lastampa:1943-01-22/p1): "Velivoli italiani a grande raggio di azione hanno agito sul porto di Orano; una nave è stata lasciata in fiamme ed un'altra gravemente danneggiata." The paper's account of the same night ("L'incursione su Orano", same page): long-range bombers that had left "una base avanzata" in the afternoon reached Oran after a long flight over the sea and, against "la violentissima reazione delle difese nemiche", bombed the crowded port; it names two crew captains, tenenti piloti Giano Rossi and Antonio D'Alò. The unit is not named. These are the attackers' claims; the battery's fire at 2100 is on the same night, which is a match by date only. The unit, from a secondary account: the 274ª Squadriglia Bombardamento a Grande Raggio's two Piaggio P.108B four-engined bombers, from Sardinia: "Il 20 gennaio i velivoli dei ten. D'Alò e Rossi chiudono questo ciclo operativo con un'impegnativa missione sul porto di Orano"; Rossi's aircraft met an enemy night fighter, which broke off (alieuomini:piaggio_p_b,71, from Garello 1973). No loss that night is recorded there. The airfield is not named (Decimomannu likely, inferred). No. 153 Squadron RAF's Beaufighters were at Maison Blanche (Algiers) that night, not Oran: P/O Benn and Sgt Lunan destroyed a Ju 88 "about 7 miles north of Algiers" (tna:AIR 27/1027/30/p11). So the night fighter that met the P.108 over Oran was another unit's (not identified).

actions.text: Fired on hostile targets 2050 to 2125 Weather good
actions.note: 4 mi W of Algiers. The city's paper reports the raid: L'Écho d'Alger, 13 May 1943 (gallica:bpt6k75870445), "Alerte à Alger": an alert in the evening, enemy aircraft over the city, "La réaction de la D.C.A. a été très violente et efficace. Quelques bombes ont été lancées." Allied communiqué no. 188 of 13 May (L'Écho d'Alger, 14 May, gallica:bpt6k7587045k): bombers that tried to attack Algiers "la nuit dernière" were driven off by the anti-aircraft guns and night fighters, "Trois appareils au moins ont été détruits", a few civilian casualties, light damage. That claim is the whole defense's, not this battery's. Neither the Italian bulletins (nos. 1083, 1084) nor the German communiqués printed in La Stampa of 14 and 15 May mention Algiers. The German Naval Staff's war diary, 12 May 1943 (skl:45/p152): "Thirty bombers raided Algiers during the night of 12 May, scoring hits on the harbor." No losses given. The RAF night fighters' record: No. 153 Squadron, Beaufighter V.8632, F/Sgt G.L. Linklater and Sgt L.V. Anthony, patrol 1935-2140, "1 JU.88 destroyed" (tna:AIR 27/1027/38/p2). The summary (tna:AIR 27/1027/37/p3): on patrol in Algiers Bay, warned of bandits 40 miles north at 16,000 ft; "The enemy aircraft which was taking evasive action from A.A. turned South about two miles West of Algiers. Our aircraft closed in and gave a two second burst. This was enough and the bandit blew up and fell into the sea. 1 Ju88 destroyed." The battery's position (4 mi W of Algiers) and fire (2050-2125) fall within that place and sortie; which guns' fire the Ju 88 was evading is not recorded (Algiers had many batteries). One aircraft of the night's raiders, by the squadron's claim.

actions.text: Fired on hostile targets 2136 to 2228 Weather good
actions.note: 4 mi W of Algiers. L'Écho d'Alger, 14 May 1943 (gallica:bpt6k7587045k), "Nouvelle alerte à Alger": an alert "hier dans la soirée", "un violent tir de barrage de la D.C.A." met the aircraft trying to fly over the city; no damage, no casualties. Neither the Italian bulletins (nos. 1083, 1084) nor the German communiqués printed in La Stampa of 14 and 15 May mention Algiers. The German Naval Staff's war diary, 13 May 1943 (skl:45/p163): "Algiers was attacked by 70 Ju 88s. Hits on six steamers were observed." Most likely this night (13/14 May), though it could restate the 12/13 May raid (inferred). No losses given. No. 153 Squadron, Beaufighter EL.162, F/Lt S.S. Duff and Sgt R. Perfect, patrol 1930-2230, "1 JU.88 probably destroyed": "although the e/a was badly 'mauled' and lost height, he did not see it fall into the sea" (tna:AIR 27/1027/38/p3; tna:AIR 27/1027/37/p3).

actions.text: Fired on enemy targets 2225 to 2235 Weather good Morale excellent
actions.note: 4 mi W of Algiers. 4 Jun 1943 was a Friday. L'Écho d'Alger, 5 Jun (gallica:bpt6k7587065b), "Alerte à Alger": an alert in the evening, "On signale des dégâts et quelques victimes"; Admiral Muselier and the inspector general of civil defence (défense passive) visited the damage. 6 Jun (gallica:bpt6k7587066r), "Après l'alerte de vendredi soir": Generals Giraud and Catroux visited the bombed quarters, Catroux calling on Muslim families who had lost their homes; the Allied GHQ communiqué: "Dans la nuit du vendredi à samedi, quelques appareils ennemis ont lâché des bombes dans la région d'Alger. Il y a eu quelques victimes ... Deux bombardiers ennemis ont été détruits." The two destroyed are the whole defense's claim, not this battery's. The Axis side: Bulletin no. 1106, issued 5 Jun (La Stampa, 6 Jun, lastampa:1943-06-06/p1): "L'aviazione dell'Asse ha bombardato questa notte il porto di Algeri." The German High Command's communiqué of 5 Jun (same page): "Le installazioni portuali di Algeri sono state bombardate la scorsa notte." The attacking unit is not named. The German Naval Staff's war diary, 4 Jun 1943 (skl:46/p38): "In the evening of 4 June 19 bombers attacked Algiers. The target was covered by a smoke screen. Two planes are missing." Two of the 19 crews did not return; no record here says what brought them down. No. 153 Squadron, Beaufighter V.8694, W/O R.J. Smith and Sgt J.J. Sanderson, scramble from Maison Blanche 2205-2325, "JU.88 destroyed" (tna:AIR 27/1027/40/p1), "15 miles North of Algiers" (tna:AIR 27/1027/39/p1). That is one of the two German crews missing that night, if the claim is right; the other is not accounted for in these records.

actions.text: The first tracks of the Battalion reached the beach at about 1030 hours, and by 1400 hours all personnel and vehicles of the Battalion were ashore and the AAA weapons were in positions in defense of the Division beaches.
actions.note: D-Day of the southern France landing (Operation Dragoon), near Sainte-Maxime. No enemy aircraft attacked the beaches that day.

actions.text: Two ME 109's flying at cruising speed in the vicinity of J-546416 was fired on by guns of Battery "D". One of the planes was definitely destroyed.
actions.note: Four detachments of Battery D were defending Battery A of the 976th FA at J-546416, near Moirans (Lambert Zone III grid). The narrative counts it as the one plane destroyed in August.

actions.text: Two ME 109's strafing from an altitude of 200 feet were engaged by Battery "D" and one of these was probably destroyed as many hits were observed. Thirteen rounds of 37mm and 1,050 rounds of 50 cal...
actions.note: Battery D's CP that day was J-552408, near Moirans.

actions.text: This Battalion engaged two ME 109's on reconnaissance flying at an approximate altitude of 50 to 75 feet. Batteries "A" and "D" expended a total of 17 rounds of 37mm and 1,100 rounds of cal. 50...
Two ME 109's ... strafed elements of the 189th Field Artillery which is defended by Battery "D" ... Numerous 50 cal. hits were observed entering the plane head-on.
actions.note: Near Baume-les-Dames (Doubs). 27 rounds of 37mm and 850 of .50 cal.

actions.text: Two ME 109's flying at an approximate altitude of 100 feet with top cover of two FW 190's. Battery "D" expended 200 rounds ... out of range of "D" Battery's guns, but seventh detachment of "D" Battery fired to warn adjacent units...

About fifty (50) Germans escaping from the south on foot, passed near the third detachment of "D" Battery in the vicinity of P-143850. The sentry on duty endeavored to halt them and fired upon them when they ran. All but six ... were captured shortly thereafter by elements of the 179th Infantry.
actions.note: Placed at the detachment's position (Lambert Zone II grid), 4.6 km east of Abbenans, where the battery's station was. The month's narrative credits the capture to "alertness of a sentry on duty at a gun section of Battery D" (p09).

actions.text: Batteries "C" and "D" engaged two ME 109's which flew at an approximate altitude of from 100 to 600 feet ... Mission of the enemy aircraft was strafing. Hits reported by both Batteries.

Two ME 109's ... strafed ... Batteries "C" and "D" expended a total of 121 rounds of 37mm and 3,375 rounds of cal. 50... One plane was observed to have burst into flames when engaged by 37mm. A 179th Infantry patrol reported plane crashed in vicinity of CHENIMENIL and pilot was dead.
actions.note: Placed at the crash, which four eyewitness certificates confirmed.

actions.text: Batteries "C" and "D" engaged one ME 109 ... at an approximate altitude of from 75 to 600 feet ... No damage reported on enemy aircraft.
This Battalion engaged 2 ME 109's on reconnaissance ... Batteries B and D expended a total of 142 rounds of 37mm and 6,440 rounds of cal. 50 ammunition in barrage fire without result.
actions.note: Near Rambervillers.

actions.text: One ME 109 ... straffed in the vicinity of Q-845275. Plane took violent evasive action when engaged. Batteries "B" and "D" expended a total of 91 rounds of 37mm and 2,250 rounds of cal. 50, "B" Battery shooting off the tail... Enemy pilot was seen to bail out over forward lines.
actions.note: Placed where the plane strafed (Obermodern). The tail is credited to Battery B.

actions.text: One ME 109 ... on armed reconnaissance was engaged by this Battalion without result. Batteries "B", "C", and "D" expended a total of 196 rounds of 37mm and 7,000 rounds...
This Battalion engaged four ME 109's which straffed in the vicinity of Zutzendorf ... Batteries "B" and "D" expended a total of 8 rounds of 37mm and 400 rounds of cal. 50 ... without result.

Eight P-47's ... bearing American markings ... committed hostile act by strafing... Batteries "A" and "D" engaged these aircraft. Battery "D" had one (1) 37mm hit and several cal. 50 hits on three other planes.
actions.note: The month's narrative (p08): the P-47s of 30 and 31 December "were discovered to have been flown by German pilots".

actions.text: Two FW 190's flying on armed reconnaissance at approximate altitude of from 1,500 to 200 feet... "D" Battery ... reported several 37mm and numerous cal. 50 hits on both planes. Pending further confirmation we claim two (2) enemy aircraft probably destroyed.

This battalion engaged one ME 109 Flying on armed reconnaissance at an altitude of from 100 to 200 feet. Battery "D" expended 30 rounds of 37mm and 1,537 rounds of cal. 50 ammunition. Plane strafed in the vicinity of R-007378.
actions.note: Placed where the plane strafed (near Wœrth).

actions.text: Two P-47's approached ... one of which flew too low and crashed ... The remaining P-47 having a red tail, circled ... and strafed... Battery D expended 35 rounds of 37mm and 1,650 rounds of cal. 50 ammunition at this aircraft in the vicinity of ZUTZENDORF.
actions.note: "Both planes were identified by Air Support Officer of 45th Infantry Division to have been friendly" (p05).

actions.text: One P-51 bearing American markings ... Plane continued to Q-7831 grid and strafed Batteries "A" and "B" of 693rd F.A. Battalion at which time 2nd Platoon of "D" Battery, this organization engaged.
actions.note: It crashed near Q-834264, killing the pilot. Whose it was isn't said.

actions.text: 2 Me 109's on armed reconnaissance over the Division Sector ... were engaged by all Batteries. Numerous 37mm and .50 Cal. hits were observed by B, C, and D Batteries on both planes. Pilot of one Me 109 bailed out... Plane crashed vic. Q-805330.
actions.note: Placed at the crash (Ingwiller). Claimed one definite and one probable; February's only engagement.

actions.text: Between 0030 and 0130 Batteries A, C, and D, engaged enemy A/C flying from 400 to 4500 feet. Plane believed to have crashed in the vicinity of M-4820. No claims.
actions.note: The night of the 45th Division's Rhine crossing near Worms. Placed at the 1 km square where the plane was believed down.

actions.text: Batteries B, C, and D engaged two (2) ME-109's on armed reconnaissance over the Division Sector... without results.

Two (2) ME-109's were engaged by all units of this battalion. Enemy aircraft strafed positions of the 189th Field Artillery Bn area and the highway in the vicinity of M-977495 without damage. Battery D observed hits and the pilot was seen to bail out... Plane was later confirmed as definitely destroyed.
One ME 262, flying at 3500 to 6000 feet on armed reconnaissance over the Division Sector, was engaged by batteries A, C, and D... without result.
actions.note: Battery D also engaged the jets with all batteries at 0655, 0713 and 1445, and with Battery B at 1133; none hit.

actions.text: Two (2) missions of one (1) ME-262 each, on armed reconnaissance flying at 1500 to 2500 feet were engaged by all batteries. Results were several .50 cal. hits observed.
A Pfc of Battery D was wounded by enemy shell fragment during a barrage.
actions.note: The record names him.

actions.text: One (1) M-16, 2nd Platoon, Battery D, fired 100 rounds of .50 cal ammunition at enemy foot troops at coordinates H-825085, wounding one (1) and capturing three (3) prisoners of war.
actions.note: Typed square H, as in the journal's Ostheim (H-775093). Falls at Eußenhausen, near Mellrichstadt.

actions.text: The 2nd Platoon, Battery D, fired four (4) ground missions at enemy foot troops in the vicinity O-2257. Results were a machine gun neutralized; fires observed; and enemy dispersed.
actions.note: Near Godeldorf (Baunach), which Battery C helped clear next day. 88 rounds of 37mm and 750 of .50 cal.

actions.text: Three men of Battery D were wounded by an 88mm shell that hit their M-15 half-track. One, a corporal, later died of his wounds.
actions.note: The record names all three. Placed with the 2nd Platoon's missions that day; the shell's position isn't given.

actions.text: There were three (3) missions of FW-190s, total of twenty-nine (29) enemy planes ... engaged by all batteries. Several hits were observed and one (1) FW-190 was seen to go down smoking in the vicinity of O-233568.
actions.note: Placed where the plane went down (Kemmern). Claimed one probable.

actions.text: Four missions by a total of six (6) ME-262s, one (1) ME-109, and six (6) FW-190s on armed reconnaissance and bombing missions ... Planes were engaged by Batteries B, C, and D. Several 37mm and .50 cal. hits were observed.
A corporal of Battery D suffered concussion as a result of friendly gun fire.
actions.note: The record names him.

actions.text: There were four (4) missions by a total of eighteen (18) enemy aircraft ... engaged by Batteries B, C, and D. Results were several 37mm and .50 cal hits observed by Battery B.
Three (3) missions by a total of four (4) JU-87s and four (4) ME-262s ... were engaged by all batteries. No hits were reported.
Six (6) ME-262s flying at 500 to 5000 feet attacking B-26 Bombers were engaged by Batteries C and D without result.
actions.note: At 1725 another Me 262 was engaged by Batteries C and D, also without result.

actions.text: One (1) M-16, 2nd Platoon, Battery D, fired at enemy personnel at coordinates T-684045. Results are unknown. Ammunition expenditures: 400 rounds .50 cal.
actions.note: Near Waidhofen (Schrobenhausen).

units.name: Medical Detachment, 67th Coast Artillery (AA) / 894th AAA AW Bn
units.note: The regiment's medical detachment: a regimental section with the Regimental HQ Battery and a section for each battalion, its men on special duty with the batteries. 2nd Bn, 67th CA (AA) became the 894th AAA AW Bn; the detachment reports as the 894th's by 19 Mar 1944. Its 1942-43 reports are book-type (roll 794, parts 2-3); March-April 1943 are missing.

stations.station: Paterson, N.J. Usual duties. Training Program.
stations.note: September 1942 (cover p0935). A book-type report, filmed sideways: one cover per month, a page of remarks for every few days, and a station page with the month in ten-day blocks. 10-17: "End of training program & assignments made." The detachment was at Paterson all summer (June, p0891).
stations.place_note: matched: Paterson, Passaic County, New Jersey, United States

stations.station: Ft. Hancock, N.J. Left Paterson, N.J. 7:30 A.M. Nov. 2, 1942 for Ft. Hancock, N.J. Distance marched 70 miles. Taking station there and performing usual camp duties with training program.
stations.note: November 1942 (cover rg64-427231553/p0997). The October report has the 1st Bn medical section going ahead to Fort Hancock and the 3rd Bn's to Teaneck, N.J., in 20-31 Oct (rg64-427231553/p0979). 11-20: usual garrison duties.
stations.place_note: Fort Hancock on Sandy Hook, N.J. (OSM matched its old radio station inside the fort).

stations.station: Left Ft. Hancock, N.J. for Camp A.P. Hill Mil. Res. Va, Taking station there and having field problems.
stations.note: Written under "20-31" (as typed; November has 30 days), so the day of the move isn't given. This is the Fort A.P. Hill the family remembers.
stations.place_note: The A.P. Hill Military Reservation, Caroline County, Va. (OSM matched it under its 2023-25 name, Fort Anderson-Pinn-Hill); a point in the reservation, not a particular camp.

stations.note: December 1942 (cover p0026). Written under "20-31"; the day isn't given (the CDSG regimental history has the regiment moving to Fort Dix on 27 Dec). 1-20: Camp A.P. Hill Mil Res Va, usual field duties.
stations.place_note: matched: Fort Dix, New Hanover Township, Burlington County, New Jersey, 08640, United States

stations.note: January 1943 (cover p0044). As written: the transport USS Ancon, in convoy UGF-4. 1-10: Ft. Dix, usual camp duties. "10-20" is the report's ten-day block. The Regimental HQ Battery's report has the dates: left Fort Dix by rail at 0730 on 13 Jan, embarked on the Ancon at the New York Port of Embarkation, Staten Island, at 1600; sailed at 0530 on 14 Jan; reached Oran at 1800 on 26 Jan, 3800 miles by water (rg64-427223420/p0730).

stations.station: Disembarked at Mers-el-Kebir at 10.00 A.M. Campsite La Senia Airport.
stations.note: Arrived by sea (convoy UGF-4). The Regimental HQ Battery has the Ancon reaching Oran at 1800 on the 26th and the men going ashore at 1000 on the 27th, marching a mile to the trucks and riding 8 miles to the bivouac (rg64-427223420/p0730). The Ancon's war diary agrees (as summarised by the 32nd Station Hospital, which crossed on her), so the detachment's "26" is probably a day early. 27-31: usual camp duties.
stations.place_note: La Sénia airfield, about 10 km south of Oran (now Ahmed Ben Bella Airport); the camp beside it isn't placed more exactly.

units.name: 60th Armored Infantry Battalion (9th Armored Division)
units.note: Part of the 9th Armored Division (etoob-9AD/p499). The positions are the battalion's own, from its monthly after action reports, October 1944 - March 1945, as transcribed by EUCMH (eucmh60aib; original in NARA RG 407), and are drawn solid. A company's move (Able Co to Distroff, 9 Feb 1945) is not the battalion's and is not a station. Transcribed so far: October 1944 - March 1945.

stations.station: in the immediate vicinity of Larochette (Fels), in central Luxembourg
stations.note: "The 60th Armored Infantry Battalion completed the last leg of its journey across France on October 20 1944. Arriving at its targeted bivouac area in the immediate vicinity of Larochette (Fels), in central Luxembourg, at 1250." Then under Combat Command A, 9th Armored Division, in bivouac for the rest of the period. In the transcription this report has no month heading; its period is taken to be October.
stations.place_note: matched: Larochette, Canton Mersch, Luxembourg

stations.station: in position relieving the 1/121 (8th Infantry Division), between the Our and Sauer Rivers
stations.note: "The relief of the 1/121 was completed on Nov 2 1944 at 1050 with our troops in position." The sector is described by its terrain ("The Our River and the Sauer River ran between the two lines"; Bollendorf and Wallendorf, Germany, named as landmarks) but no village for the battalion is named, so no place is given. The battalion was in bivouac near Larochette before (the major portion of its transportation stayed there), and was relieved by the 1/121 on 9 Nov at 1230; where it went then is not stated (the report is headed "Day's location : 60-AIB, December 5 1944, Steinsel - Heisdorf, Luxembourg").

stations.station: in tactical bivouac in vicinity of Larochette (Fels)
stations.note: "From Dec 1 to Dec 9, the 60-AIB was assigned to CCA, 9-AD. ... Approximately half of the unit was in tactical bivouac in vicinity of Larochette (Fels), and the remainder in billets in and around Heisdorf." Position for the first half; the other half at Heisdorf.
stations.place_note: matched: Larochette, Canton Mersch, Luxembourg

stations.station: a sector of the line assigned to 9-AD (relieving the 2/109)
stations.note: "By Dec 10, at 1110, the battalion completed relieving the 2/109, in a sector of the line assigned to 9-AD." No place is named for the sector. On 16 Dec the report puts the German attack through the draws at Dilligen and Grundhof, with the front companies at Beaufort, Luxembourg, by 17 Dec.

stations.station: Battalion Motor Park in the vicinity of Savelborn
stations.note: "With the enemy in control of Beaufort ... at 1743, the Hq & Hq Co (minus) withdrew to the Battalion Motor Park in the vicinity of Savelborn." Headquarters company only; the rifle companies were cut off at Beaufort and the front line, and the report gives no single battalion position for them. Not mapped: the position is the headquarters company's, and no battalion position is given.
"The 60-AIB's CP was moved to 9136" (19 Dec), on the defensive line Waldbillig - Ermsdorf. A four-figure reference with no map sheet or place: not placed.

"At 1600, Dec 26, the 60-AIB was relieved in the Savelborn sector and as part of CCA, 9-AD, moved immediately to Longlier, Belgium. Arriving at 2345, CCA, was attached to the 4th Armored Division." The report writes "Dec 19" for the following day's attack (8 o'clock, along the Neufchateau - Bastogne road); the context makes it 27 Dec.
stations.place_note: matched: Longlier, Neufchâteau, Luxembourg, Wallonia, Belgium

stations.station: the high ground north of Sibret
stations.note: Task Force Collins (the battalion less Baker Co, with attachments): "Upon taking Sibret our direction of advance was changed ... to secure the high ground north of Sibret which was accomplished by night fall, December 27." At darkness road blocks surrounded Sibret and Able Co occupied the high ground north of it.
stations.place_note: matched: Sibret, Vaux-sur-Sûre, Bastogne, Luxembourg, Wallonia, Belgium

stations.station: the high ground south of the town (Chenogne)
stations.note: 30 Dec: Task Force Collins took Chenogne; "At darkness our troops pulled back and occupied the high ground south of the town". Attacked from Chenogne on 31 Dec at 0530; Charlie Co fell back to a reserve position just north of Sibret and "By noon our troops had been reorganized and the line firmly established." No distance from the town is given.
stations.place_note: matched: Chenogne, Vaux-sur-Sûre, Bastogne, Luxembourg, Wallonia, 6640, Belgium

stations.station: the high ground immediately north of Sibret, Belgium
stations.note: "From midnight to early morning, January 1 1945, Task Force Collins, as part of CCA-9-AD, held the high ground immediately north of Sibret, Belgium." It attacked at 1100 toward the high ground south of the railroad between Chenogne and Senonchamps and was "digging in on its objective" within five or six hours (no place named for it beyond that). CCA was relieved by the 17th Airborne Division on the afternoon of 3 Jan.
stations.place_note: matched: Sibret, Vaux-sur-Sûre, Bastogne, Luxembourg, Wallonia, Belgium

stations.station: in the vicinity of Volaiville, Belgium
stations.note: "Immediately the 60-AIB began its march to the rear, spending the night, January 4, in the vicinity of Volaiville, Belgium." The same report later has the march resuming "on the morning of January 4 from the vicinity of Volaiville", so its own dates disagree; the relief was on 3 Jan.
stations.place_note: matched: Volaiville, Léglise, Neufchâteau, Luxembourg, Wallonia, 6860, Belgium

stations.station: bivouac in and around the town of Veil-Saint-Rémy, between Rethel and Charleville-Méizières, France
stations.note: "That night the 60-AIB closed into bivouac in and around the town of Veil-Saint-Rémy, between Rethel and Charleville-Méizières, France." The report puts the night at Volaiville on both 3 and 4 Jan, and the arrival here "that night" after leaving Volaiville on the 4th: so the 4th or the 5th. The date drawn is the 5th.
stations.place_note: matched by hand: Viel-Saint-Remy, Rethel, Ardennes, Grand Est, France, 08270 (the transcription spells it Veil-Saint-Rémy; the first query, with the spelling Vieil, found nothing). Between Rethel and Charleville-Mézières, as the report says

stations.station: a bivouac area in and near Metzeresche, France
stations.note: "The next, January 12, the march was resumed with the 60-AIB closing into a bivouac area in and near Metzeresche, France. We occupied this area during the reminder of January." Reconstituting supplies, reconditioning and receiving equipment, and intensive training. The division's command post was at Bockange, then Ennery (etoob-9AD/p503-504).
stations.place_note: matched: Metzeresche, Thionville, Moselle, Grand Est, Metropolitan France, 57920, France

stations.station: new billet areas near Trooz, Belgium
stations.note: "At 0700, February 23, the 60-AIB, began marching from its billet areas in the vicinity of Metzeresche, France, to new billet areas near Trooz, Belgium, closing in the new areas at 2315 after a march of 186 miles." From 1 to 22 Feb the companies were "in billets in and near Metzeresche"; on 9 Feb Able Co (a company, not the battalion) moved from Mancy (Bettelainville) to Distroff, France, so no row for that. The battalion command post was at Trooz on 28 Feb.
stations.place_note: matched: Trooz, Liège, Wallonia, 4870, Belgium

stations.station: assembly area in the village of Drove (Kreuzau), Germany
stations.note: "The march began at 1215, with the battalion marching as part of CCA 9-AD, and at 2130 the battalion closed into its assembly area at Drove (Kreuzau), Germany." The commanding officer was placed in command of Task Force Collins at 2200, for an attack the next day.
stations.place_note: matched: Drove, Kreuzau, Kreis Düren, North Rhine-Westphalia, 52372, Germany

stations.station: marching in vehicles toward its objective, Wollersheim (Nideggen); the advance guard crossed the Line of Departure, Berg (Nideggen), at 0700
stations.note: "Early morning, March 1, Task Force Collins began marching in vehicles toward its objective, Wollersheim (Nideggen), with the advance guard, Baker 60-AIB and 1 Plat 19-TB attached, crossing the Line of Departure, Berg (Nideggen), Germany, at 0700." Task Force Collins was the battalion less Charlie Co (with attachments). Only the advance guard (Baker Co) is placed at Berg; the report gives no position for the battalion as a whole that day (Able Co and Baker Co were pinned down near Wollersheim by night). Not mapped. The battalion had closed into Drove on 28 Feb.

stations.station: in position west of Wollersheim (Nideggen), Germany
stations.note: "After being cleared, the town was occupied for the night by Able Co and out posted on the high ground to the east by Charlie Co, while the remainder of the Task Force remained in position west of the town." The town was officially cleared at 1715 on 2 Mar. Task Force Collins, the battalion with attachments (Charlie Co 60-AIB joined it that morning). No distance from the town is given.
stations.place_note: matched: Wollersheim, Nideggen, Kreis Düren, North Rhine-Westphalia, 52385, Germany

stations.station: Wollersheim (Nideggen), Germany: Task Force Collins less Charlie Co
stations.note: "When Charlie Co ( ) began its move, the remainder of Task Force Collins occupied Wollerscheim." Charlie Co moved east and occupied Langendorf at 0845 (a company, not the battalion, so no row for Langendorf). The Task Force stayed at Wollersheim until its move on 4 Mar.
stations.place_note: matched: Wollersheim, Nideggen, Kreis Düren, North Rhine-Westphalia, 52385, Germany

stations.station: moving at noon to the Line of Departure, Oberelvenich (Zülpich) to Nemmenich (Zülpich), to attack Euskirchen
stations.note: "At noon, March 4, the Task Force, in column, began its move toward a Line of Departue, Oberelvenich (Zülpich) to Nemmenich (Zülpich), with the mission of clearing the north edge of Euskirchen and seizing a crossing on the Erft River in its zone of action." The attack was then launched with Able and Charlie Cos abreast; the report gives no battalion position other than this line, which is a line, not a place. Not mapped. The bridge over the Erft in Euskirchen had been blown when the Task Force arrived that day.

stations.station: Euskirchen, Germany (its portion of the town), with a bridgehead over the Erft
stations.note: "On March 5, Task Force Collins finished and occupied its portion of Euskirchen and maintained the bridgehead while constructed a crossing over the Erft River." Able and Charlie Cos had established the bridgehead at 0500; at 2145 Charlie Co attacked across the Erft toward Palmersheim (a company, so no row).
stations.place_note: matched: Kreis Euskirchen, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany (the district, whose point is at the town); checked: the point is the town of Euskirchen

stations.station: Odendorf, Germany: Task Force Collins less Charlie Co 60-AIB, closing at 0755
stations.note: "On the morning of March 6, the Task Force less Charlie 60-AIB and the 1st Plat of Able 19-TB, moved from Euskirchen to Odendorf, closing at 0755 where it received orders to continue the attack of CCA-9-AD passing through friendly units at Rheinbach as soon as that town had been cleared." It crossed the Line of Departure in Rheinbach at 1300; the advance guard took Wormersdorf (2100) and Charlie Co Ersdorf (2220), companies, so no rows for them.
stations.place_note: matched: Odendorf, Swisttal, Rhein-Sieg-Kreis, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany

stations.station: Lantershofen, Germany (the balance of the Task Force closed in at 0205)
stations.note: "At this point, Task Force Collins halted with Baker and Charlie Cos occupying defensive positions on the high ground just east of the town, and the balance of the Task Force closed into Lantershofen." Baker Co passed through Charlie Co at Lantershofen at 0205. A PW collection point and the battalion CP were there; Able Co relieved Charlie Co in its defensive sector at 1535 on 7 Mar. The Task Force had halted "early the next morning" (7 Mar) after the night march from Odendorf.
stations.place_note: matched: Lantershofen, Grafschaft, Landkreis Ahrweiler, Rhineland-Palatinate, 53501, Germany

stations.station: Sinzig, Germany: the Task Force moved in at 0645; Able and Charlie Cos on the high ground south of the town
stations.note: "On March 8, at 0645, the Task Force moved into Sinzig and by noon Able and Charlie 60-AIB occupied defensive positions on the high ground south of the town." Mission: protecting the Remagen Bridgehead in a sector west of the Rhine. The battalion was relieved from defensive positions by the 23-IR (2-ID) on 9 Mar afternoon, took a new sector on the west bank (Able Co, 0400, 10 Mar), was relieved again on 11 Mar and put on alert. "During the period March 8-12, when the companies were not defending a sector in the vicinity of Sinzig, their time was consumed in receiving, processing and training reinforcement": the battalion stayed at Sinzig until 12 Mar.
stations.place_note: matched: Sinzig, Landkreis Ahrweiler, Rhineland-Palatinate, 53489, Germany

stations.station: crossing the Rhine on a pontoon bridge in the vicinity of Kripp, about 2000 meters southeast of the Ludendorff bridge
stations.note: "Effective March 12, 1800, the 60-AIB was attached to CCB-9-AD. Immediately orders were received to move the battalion to the vicinity of Unkel, and at 2025, the battalion began marching from Sinzig closing in its new assembly area at 2315. During this march the battalion crossed the Rhine River, using a pontoon bridge constructed by US Army Engineers in the vicinity of Kripp, approximately 2000 meters southeast of the main Ludendorff bridge in Remagen." The crossing was between 2025 and 2315; the time is not given.
stations.place_note: matched: Kripp, Remagen, Landkreis Ahrweiler, Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany

stations.station: assembly area east of the Rhine, in the vicinity of Unkel (closed in at 2315)
stations.note: "Immediately orders were received to move the battalion to the vicinity of Unkel, and at 2025, the battalion began marching from Sinzig closing in its new assembly area at 2315." The report does not say the assembly area was in Unkel itself: it names the vicinity of Unkel as the destination, so this row is at the town only to that extent. "Upon closing into its first assembly area east of the Rhine River, the 60-AIB was attached to the 311-IR (78-ID)." It was then ordered to Rheinbreitbach "for a short time" on 13 Mar (arrival not stated), then to Bad Honnef.
stations.place_note: matched: Unkel, Landkreis Neuwied, Rhineland-Palatinate, 53572, Germany

stations.station: Bad Honnef, Germany: securing the town, a defensive sector near its northeastern edge
stations.note: "On March 13, the battalion was ordered to Rheinbreitbach, for a short time and then to Bad Honnef where it was assigned the mission of securing the town which had been taken by another unit that day." Defensive sector near the northeastern edge of the town; "At 1700 all companies were ordered back into town and established a system of road blocks." On 14-15 Mar the three rifle companies attacked separate hill objectives north and east of Bad Honnef (Objectives #14, #15, #16, #17, Perlenhardt, Margarethenhof): company positions, so no battalion row for them.
stations.place_note: matched: Bad Honnef, Rhein-Sieg-Kreis, North Rhine-Westphalia, 53604, Germany

stations.station: attacking Ittenbach from Objective #16 (Able and Charlie Cos abreast; Baker Co in battalion reserve)
stations.note: "Able and Charlie Cos abreast jumped off at 0910 ... Baker Co was then ordered to occupy Objective #16 as battalion reserve." Able Co gained "that portion of the city west of the creek" by 1515; Charlie Co was held out of its objective that night and the German commander surrendered the town to Charlie Co at about 1000-1200 on 17 Mar. The report puts no battalion command post in Ittenbach, but "Upon leaving Ittenbach the battalion marched to Bad Honnef", so the battalion was there when it was relieved (1900, by the 2/310-IR, 78-ID, on the night after the surrender, 17 Mar). Placed at the town on the strength of that sentence; Objective #16 (Margarethenhof) is not placed.
stations.place_note: matched: Ittenbach, Döttscheid, Gräfenhohn, Königswinter, Rhein-Sieg-Kreis, North Rhine-Westphalia,

stations.station: Bad Honnef, Germany: the battalion closed in at 2330 on its march from Ittenbach
stations.note: "Upon leaving Ittenbach the battalion marched to Bad Honnef closing in at 2330. There it received orders to move to the vicinity of Linz the next morning at 0700 and over the same route used in its march to Bad Honnef." Relieved from attachment to the 311-IR (78-ID) at 1900 and reverted to CCB-9-AD.
stations.place_note: matched: Bad Honnef, Rhein-Sieg-Kreis, North Rhine-Westphalia, 53604, Germany

stations.station: the vicinity of Linz, Germany (the movement completed on 18 Mar)
stations.note: "This movement was completed on March 18 at 111." (The hour is as transcribed, evidently a typing error.) "During the period March 18-21, the battalion was out of contact with the enemy": maintenance, reinforcements, a few men sent to Paris on 3 day passes. Attached to CCA-9-AD in place on 19 Mar at 2400; back under CCB on 21 Mar at 1200.
stations.place_note: matched: Linz am Rhein, Landkreis Neuwied, Rhineland-Palatinate, 53545, Germany

stations.station: assembly area in the vicinity of Hammerstein, Germany (closed in at 0350)
stations.note: "Receiving orders during the night of March 21 to move to an assembly area in the vicinity of Hammerstein in preparation for an attack early the next morning. The battalion moved at 0230 closing into its assigned area at 0350." The three rifle companies then moved dismounted at 0600 toward the Wied River, and Charlie Co crossed it at 1830 on a foot bridge (the river crossing is not placed to a village in the report). On 23-24 Mar the companies advanced in short moves; the report names no place for the battalion again until Bendorf on 25 Mar.
stations.place_note: matched: Hammerstein, Bad Hönningen, Landkreis Neuwied, Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany

stations.station: Bendorf, Germany: Baker, Able and Charlie Cos crossed the Saynbach and entered the town (1110)
stations.note: "The main body of the Task Force crossed the ine of Departue at 0500, and by 1110, Baker 60-AIB followed by Able 60-AIB, supported by fire from Baker 14-TB, succeeded in crossing the river over small foot bridge and entered Bendorf." Charlie Co and the tanks then crossed on the main highway bridge between Engers and Bendorf and moved south, bypassing Weitersburg. A passage through the town on the way south, not a stay.
stations.place_note: matched: Bendorf, Landkreis Mayen-Koblenz, Rhineland-Palatinate, 56170, Germany

stations.station: Vallendar, Germany, and the high ground beyond it (the battalion's final objective), the three rifle companies in and around the town
stations.note: "By 2000, the northern edge of Vallendar had been cleared, and Baker Co moved in. Charlie Co continued its mission of clearing the town and completed it shortly before midnight. At 0400, Able Co reported all AA guns destroyed and the 60-AIB's final objective occupied." The final objective was the high ground (the Mallendarer Berg). Relieved in place by the 27-AIB by noon on 26 Mar; no battalion command post is named, so the place is the town the companies cleared.
stations.place_note: matched: Vallendar, Landkreis Mayen-Koblenz, Rhineland-Palatinate, 56179, Germany

stations.station: the west bank of the Lahn River opposite Diez, Germany (reached at 1950)
stations.note: "CCA ordered the 60-AIB to continue its advance on route Yellow to the Lahn River in Diez. Reaching the west bank of the Lahn at 1950 without opposition, the 60-AIB met there its first resistance from a group of stubborn enemy dug in on the east bank of the river." All bridges were blown. Mapped at the town of Diez, but the battalion was on the bank opposite it (the report places the enemy on the east bank).
stations.place_note: matched: Diez, Rhein-Lahn-Kreis, Rhineland-Palatinate, 65582, Germany

stations.station: in and around Diez, Germany, Able and Baker Cos in defensive positions around the town
stations.note: "Able and Baker Cos then took up defensive positions around the town." Able Co crossed the Lahn at the south edge of Diez on a barge and cleared the town; Baker and Charlie Cos had been sent north to the vicinity of Limburg. "The battalion remained in position until 1115, March 28, when it was relieved in place by the 2nd Ranger Battalion." All movement orders were cancelled for 24 hours at mid-afternoon on 27 Mar.
stations.place_note: matched: Diez, Rhein-Lahn-Kreis, Rhineland-Palatinate, 65582, Germany

stations.station: Hofen (Runkel), Germany: the battalion less Charlie Co closed in at 2000
stations.note: "At 1400, CCA began moving to the new assembly area with the 60-AIB less Charlie Co marching near the end of the column behind seven other units. ... At 2000, the battalion closed into Hofen and immediately set up road blocks and a system of all-round security for the night." Charlie Co was attached to CCA and sent to Aumenau to relieve elements of CCB-9-AD protecting a Lahn bridgehead (a company, so no row for Aumenau). The report says only "Hofen"; the assembly area was to be in the vicinity of Hofen (Runkel).
stations.place_note: matched: Hofen, Runkel, Landkreis Limburg-Weilburg, Hesse, 65594, Germany

stations.station: billets at Oberhausen (the report names no district), closed in at 1945
stations.note: "The 60-AIB closed into billets at Oberhausen at 1945 and set up security for the night awaiting orders for the next day." The CCA column had left Hofen at 0600 for the vicinity of Hausen and by noon was ordered on to phase line Denver. No district or county is given for Oberhausen, and several places bear the name; none could be matched to this march with confidence, so the row is in the log and not on the map.

stations.station: within 3000 meters of Fritzlar by 1330; the battalion in the attack on the town and its airfield
stations.note: "The attack moved to within 3000 meters of its objective by 1330 with only one delay of an hour and a half at Treysa due to sniper fire. 3000 meters outside Fritzlar the enemy had a 150-MM AT gun and a 20-MM AA gun serving as an outpost for an airfield just south of the Eder River." The planned Line of Departure was Kirtorf at 0600 (the Letter of Instructions; not stated as done). Able Co and tanks went to the airfield; Baker Co to Wega on the Eder (1350); Charlie Co at 2200 held a few houses on the northeastern edge of Fritzlar. Mapped at the town: the battalion was in and around it.
stations.place_note: matched: Fritzlar, Schwalm-Eder-Kreis, Hesse, 34560, Germany

stations.station: Fritzlar, Germany: relieved by the 27-AIB by 1515
stations.note: "The 27-AIB moved into Fritzlar with the mission of relieving the 60-AIB, and by 1515 the relief was complete even though part of the city north of the river had not been entirely cleared." Able and Charlie Cos held ground around the town from 0500; Baker Co moved to the southern outskirts at 0700 and then left to join the 14-TB at 1300.
stations.place_note: matched: Fritzlar, Schwalm-Eder-Kreis, Hesse, 34560, Germany

stations.station: on the road toward the assembly area in the vicinity of Wettesingen, a few miles from it at midnight
stations.note: "Upon relief the 60-AIB and attachments less Baker Co began marching toward the new assembly area in the vicinity of Wettesingen Due to darkness and heavy traffic on the roads, the column moved very slowly and was a few miles from Wettesingen at midnight." No bearing is given, so no offset; Wettesingen is the destination, not a station. Not mapped.

routes.note: Route not in the reports, drawn approximately. Sailing from Gourock on 1 Nov and arriving at Mers El Kébir on 11 Nov fits convoy KMF 2 (Clyde 1 Nov, North Africa 11–12 Nov 1942). Like the other Torch convoys it is drawn down the Firth of Clyde, through the North Channel, west round Ireland, far out into the Atlantic away from U-boats and aircraft, and east through the Strait of Gibraltar. The exact track isn't known.

Route not in the reports, drawn approximately: out past Sandy Hook, south of Nova Scotia and Newfoundland, across the North Atlantic, round the north of Ireland and up the Firth of Clyde to Greenock. The Queen Elizabeth crossed alone, without escort, relying on her speed; she took about five days (sailed 31 Aug 10:05, anchored at Greenock 5 Sep 19:00).

Rail route not in the reports, drawn approximately. They say only that the battery entrained and then boarded lorries; the stops (Glasgow, Carlisle, Crewe, Birmingham, Oxford, Reading, Pewsey) are a guess from the 1940s rail network, and the line from Greenock to Glasgow is not traced. The reported times (entrained 0230, arrived 0330) are too short for about 400 miles and were probably typed loosely. The route runs well to the west of London.

By rail from Fort Dix to the Staten Island piers (13 Jan 1943), then convoy UGF-4: out past Sandy Hook on 14 Jan, southeast to a rendezvous, a few hundred miles north of Bermuda on the 16th, east across the Atlantic, British and Canadian escorts joining west of Gibraltar on the morning of the 25th, through the Strait that night, into Mers-el-Kébir on the evening of the 26th. Dates from the Regimental HQ Battery's report and the Ancon's war diary as summarised by the 32nd Station Hospital (32ndstationhospital.com); the mid-ocean track is a guess.
